description: We learned that definite integrals give us the area under the curve and above the x-axis. But what if the curve itself is below the x-axis? In this case, the definite integral is still related to area, but it's negative. See how this works and get some intuition for why this is so.
title: Negative definite integrals

description: Since definite integrals are the net area between a curve and the x-axis, we can sometimes use geometric area formulas to find definite integrals. See how it's done.
title: Finding definite integrals using area formulas

description: Practice evaluating definite integrals by finding the area using shapes (like rectangles & circles) under a function.
